 Order
Heard on admission.

1. This M.Cr.C. under Section 528 of BNSS, 2023 (section 482 Cr.P.C.) is directed against the order dated 1.4.2024 passed in SCATR 64/2024 by the Special Judge (Atrocities Act 1989) whereby the learned Trial Court has taken the cognizance against the petitioner inviolation of the provisions of section 218 of the BNSS as well as for quashing the private complaint filed by the respondent no.2 against the petitioner.

2. Brief facts of the case are that a private complaint has been lodged against the present petitioners and other Police Officials alleging that on 6.1.2022 one Lakhan Singh Bhil with an intent to outrage the modesty of sister of complainant had entered the house and had caught hold of her hand.

When the complainant and his sister went to P.S. Janjali to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24447 2 MCRC-37166-2025 report the matter they were driven out and no complaint was registered.

3. The complainant made a complaint of the incident at C.M. Helpline and pursuance to said complaint the complainant and his sister were called on 14.3.2022 at Police Station, but the crime Kamlesh Kumar Gond vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173270180/
1 was not registered.

On 16.3.2022, when the complainant and his sister went to Police Station to fetch the copy of the report, they were pressurized to take back their complaint from C.M. Helpline,
but when they refused petitioner and other officials beat them up with belt, stick, kicks and fists and chappals and also hurled filthy abuses and uttered caste related terms.

4. In the complaint it is also averred that complaint was also made to Tribal Organisation, Guna,
which was forwarded to S.P. Guna, D.G.P. Bhopal, Human Rights Commission and Hon'ble Governor, but no action upon the complaint was taken.

5. After recording statements of complainant and his sister under section 200 and 202 of Cr.P.C.
prima facie case under section 323, 342 of IPC and sections 3 (2) (va) of SC ST Act were found and cognizance was taken by learned Court below.
Aggrieved, the present petition had been filed challenging the same.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner had argued before this Court that in order to seek personal vendetta for not registering the FIR with regard to outraging the modesty of complainant sister, just to create pressure, the complaint had been filed and learned Court below without considering this fact had taken cognizance, which is perse illegal.
7.

Further if the allegations in the complaint are taken in totality, they NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24447 3 MCRC-37166-2025 do not disclose any offence, thus the cognizance taken is bad in law and the private complaint being without sum and substance deserves to be thrown out.
8.

It was also argued that no previous sanction as required under section 197 of Cr.P.C. from the appropriate Government had been taken before taking cognizance in the matter and proceeding with it which makes the complaint vulnerable and liable to be dismissed.

To bolster his submissions he had placed reliance in the matter of Pukhraj Vs. State of Rajasthan and another, AIR 1973 SC 2591, D. Devarja Vs. Owais Sabeer Hussain, 2020 (7) SCC 695, Baijnath Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, AIR 1966 SC 220 and G.C. Manjunath and others Vs. Seetaram, 2025 3 Supreme 755 .

sentences.text: On the basis of above arguments it was prayed that petition be allowed and the order taking cognizance be set aside and the private complaint be quashed.
9. Per contra learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made in the petition and prays for its rejection.

10. With regard to the act of the petitioner and other police officials do not come within their official duty the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Chandan Kumar Basu v. State of Bihar reported in (2014)
13 SCC 70 in para 9 held as under :-

State of Punjab & Ors. reported in (2007) 1 SCC 1, it has been consistently held that it can be no part of the duty of a public servant or acting in the discharge of his official duties to commit any of the offences covered by Section 406, 409, 420 etc. and the official status of the public servant can, at best,
only provide an opportunity for commission of the offences.

Notwithstanding the above, the High Court had granted liberty to the appellant to raise the issue of sanction, if so required,
depending on the evidence that may come on record in the course of the trial.

Despite the view taken by this Court in the series of pronouncements referred to above, the opportunity that has been provided by the High Court to the benefit of the appellant need not be foreclosed by us inasmuch as in Matajog Dobey vs. H.C. Bhari reported in (1955) 2 SCR 925, P.K. Pradhan vs. State of Sikkim reported in 2001 (6) SCC 704 and Prakash Singh Badal (supra) this Court had consistently held that the question of sanction under Section 197 of the Code can be raised at any time after cognizance had been taken and may have to be determined at different stages of the proceeding/trial.

sentences.text: The observations of this Court in this regard may be usefully extracted below.
Matajog Dobey vs. H.C. Bhari (para 21) "The question may arise at any stage of the proceedings.

The complaint may not disclose that the act constituting the offence was done or purported to be done in the discharge of official duty; but facts subsequently coming to light on a police or judicial inquiry or even in the course of the prosecution evidence at the trial, may establish the necessity for sanction.
Whether sanction is necessary or not may have to be determined from stage to stage.
The necessity may reveal itself in the course of the progress of the case."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24447 5 MCRC-37166-2025 P.K. Pradhan vs. State of Sikkim (para 15)

entities.text: P.K. Pradhan vs. State of Sikkim
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "It is well settled that question of sanction under Section 197 of the Code can be raised any time after the cognizance; may be immediately after cognizance or framing of charge or even at the time of conclusion of trial and after conviction as well.

But there may be certain cases where it may not be possible to decide the question effectively without giving opportunity to the defence to establish that what he did was in discharge of official duty.

In order to come to the conclusion whether claim of the accused, that the act that he did was in course of the performance of his duty was reasonable one and neither pretended nor fanciful, can be examined during the course of trial by giving opportunity to the defence to establish it.
In such an eventuality, the question of sanction should be left open to be decided in the main judgment which may be delivered upon conclusion of the trial."
Prakash Singh Badal & Anr. vs. State of Punjab & Ors.

] "The question relating to the need of sanction under Section 197 of the Code is not necessarily to be considered as soon as the complaint is lodged and on the allegations contained therein.
This question may arise at any stage of the proceeding.

11. From the above it is clear that the act of the petitioner and other police officials do not come within their official duty, therefore, prior sanction for their prosecution is not required and the rest findings arrived at by the learned Court below that prima facie case is made out and cognizance is therefore taken is not bad in law.
12.

Upon perusal of the impugned order, this Court is of the considered view that the Court below upon proper evaluation of facts and evidence on record has passed the impugned order applying correct NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24447 6 MCRC-37166-2025 principles of law.
13. There is no illegality or jurisdictional error warranting interference in inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 528 of BNSS, 2023.
14. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. is hereby dismissed.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE (aspr)
